content: IPv6 zero compression follows RFC 5952 canonical form: drop leading zeros per group, replace only the single longest run of all-zero groups with ::, never compress a single zero group, and use lowercase hex. /127 point-to-point links and /128 host routes have zero usable host bits - broadcast/network-address concepts from IPv4 do not apply cleanly to IPv6 (no broadcast address in IPv6 at all). BigInt/128-bit arithmetic is required for IPv6 host counts since JS numbers lose precision above 2^53.
